_why: CP-5.2 rung 2. The contract's END state is the tool's own `_meta`, published by the owning service (CP-5.md §4). This file is the INTERIM home so a contract is authorable without waiting on another team — the same correction §3a/W1 already took for the ref/resolver map: 'a registry row, authored once and later pushed upstream into _meta when the owning service catches up'. `_meta` WINS wherever a service supplies it, and `Completeness.source` records which one answered so an owner-published contract and one we wrote never merge into one indistinguishable row.

identifier_resolution.book_id: an opaque id; resolve a book NAME with book_search before calling. No resolver is declared for it yet — 5.3 builds the ref/resolver map, and until it does a name here is refused rather than guessed.
identifier_resolution.chapter_id: an opaque id obtained from this same tool with kind=chapters.

argument_supplier.kind: model — the caller chooses what to list
argument_supplier.book_id: context | plan — the ambient book when the surface is book-bound (`_meta.scope: book`), otherwise a plan-bound value
argument_supplier.chapter_id: plan — emitted by a prior kind=chapters listing
argument_supplier.offset: plan — the runtime advances it while paging

repeat_semantics.signal_retained: A repeat MAY be served from cache to remove its cost. It is still COUNTED and the breaker still escalates — removing a repeat's signal is what turned a 393-call loop into 393 silent successes (§3).

error_contract.message: required on every failure; a failure carrying no message is unrepresentable

output_contract.shape: { books: [{book_id, title, access_level, chapter_count, lifecycle_state, original_language}], total }
output_contract.note: Declared so a CP-3 `emits` path is checkable at PLAN-BUILD time rather than failing at execution (§2).
output_contract._verified_against: a RECORDED result in loreweave_chat, 2026-08-10. The first draft of this member was written from the tool's DESCRIPTION and was wrong for 4 of 5 tools — a declared shape nobody checks is a lie that looks like a contract, which is exactly what §2 says the emits check is for.

result_completeness.surface: The runtime must surface is_complete=false to the model. A truncated page read as the whole answer is the quiet failure this member exists for — it appears in no error bucket.

tool_list._why: THE most-repeated tool in the corpus: 1,180 repeat-breaker firings across 3 sessions, worst session 566. Its repeat_semantics member is where section 3's rule is most load-bearing.

repeat_semantics.signal_retained: The breaker short-circuits before dispatch, so the COST is already gone. The repeat is still COUNTED (repeat_count) and the breaker still ESCALATES; the call records call_outcome=refused, never a silent success. Serving it quietly would turn 566 loud repeats into 566 invisible ones — the metric laundering section 3 exists to refuse.

identifier_resolution.book_id: an opaque id, not a name. This tool is itself the RESOLVER for EntityRef (see contracts/agent-runtime-ref-resolvers.json); it does not consume entity names in id fields.

repeat_semantics.signal_retained: A repeated identical search is counted and escalates; it is never served silently.

result_completeness._KNOWN_GAP: 🔴 THIS TOOL DOES NOT REPORT COMPLETENESS, and the contract records that rather than claiming a field that does not exist. Measured 2026-08-10: of 36 tools declaring paging, five never report it, and this is one of them — it returns at most `limit` rows with no is_complete, so a full page is indistinguishable from a truncated one.
result_completeness.runtime_compensation: CP-5.3 treats a page whose EXACT matches fill it as `truncated` and REFUSES rather than substituting, because 'exactly one match' is only true if the list was whole.
result_completeness.closes_when: glossary-service returns page{total,returned,is_complete}; the resolver then believes it and this gap entry is deleted.
